title: Geo-aware tenant fair-share windowing and fallback for limiter outages
creator: Anika Patel
description:
Problem: During regional degradation and limiter-control-plane outages we observe unfair token consumption across tenants and noisy neighbor effects. Existing fallback paths either allow large tenants to hoard burst credits or apply blunt global caps that break latency-sensitive customers. This ticket designs and implements a geo-aware "soft-slice" windowing algorithm + deterministic eviction vector and a lightweight stateless fallback controller to preserve SLOs and fairness during limiter outages and multi-region failovers.

Goals: (1) Maintain p99 tail latency SLOs within 10% of baseline for critical tenants during cross-region failover, (2) Bound emergency error budget burn per tenant, (3) Ensure fairness — small tenants should not be starved by large tenants during degraded modes, (4) Provide clear rollback and observability for incidents.
acceptance_criteria: Canary deployment (10% traffic) shows p99 latency ≤ 110% of baseline and token cost variance ≤ 15% for top 20 tenants over 30m
Failover simulation (region A outage) demonstrates fair-share windowing prevents any tenant consuming >2x normal capacity during 60s stabilization
Emergency fallback controller engages automatically within 15s of limiter-control-plane health loss and routes to degraded caps with preserved per-tenant weighted priorities
Dashboards show new metrics: geo_slice_utilization, eviction_score_p99, fallback_activation_count and are wired to alerts
Load test artifact and runbook documented in linked design doc and PR linked in ticket
implementation_notes: Introduce 'soft-slice' windows: each region calculates per-tenant soft shares based on historical 5m demand, configured tenant weight, and region capacity; windows are fractional to allow fine-grained redistribution.
Eviction vector: deterministic 3-tuple (tenant_weight, short_term_burst, tenant_latency_penalty) hashed with region salt to ensure stable ordering across nodes during redistribution.
Lease redistribution: when control plane missing, workers exchange compact checkpoints via existing gossip channel (delta encoding) and apply proportional refill heuristics to avoid cliff effects.
Fallback controller: stateless shim that applies conservative static caps derived from recent 1h consumption percentiles; keeps a small emergency bucket for new customers to prevent hard blocks.
Circuit-breaker policy: trigger when control-plane heartbeat misses >2 heartbeats OR error_budget_burn_rate > 5x baseline; automatic rollback to previous policy after 5min of healthy heartbeats.
Observability: emit standardized tags (region, tenant_id, policy_mode) and new metrics; sample 1% of requests in fallback mode for detailed traces to Sentry/Tracing.
Performance constraints: new path must add <2% CPU on serving runtime and <3ms p50 added latency on common codepaths; microbenchmarks required before canary.
test_plan: Unit tests for eviction ranking and lease arithmetic (edge cases: overflow, negative refill)
Integration test: simulated multi-region failover in staging using chaos monkey (region shutdown) verifying redistribution correctness
Load test: synthetic mix of 500 tenants with Pareto distribution of traffic; measure fairness score and SLO delta over 60m
Canary rollout: 10% production for 30m, monitor p99 latency, error budget burn, fallback activation; escalate at thresholds
Postmortem drill: run tabletop with SRE/SE/PM using staging incident data to validate runbook clarity
rollback_plan: Immediate rollback to 'global-static-cap' policy via feature flag; if rollback fails, route traffic to Dedicated pools for affected customers using regional routing policy. Contact on-call (pager) and open incident channel with runbook checklist.
